findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed there was not paper towels at the hand washing sink when the inspector arrived. The PIC provided paper towels to the hand sink during the inspection. Ensure there is always paper towels available at every hand washing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed eggs stored over milk in the lobby cooler. The PIC moved the eggs below the milk during the inspection. The inspector reminded the PIC that ready-to-eat foods must always be stored above raw foods to prevent contamination. Ensure foods are always stored according to the proper storage order.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm during the inspection. The PIC dumped and remade the solution which tested at 150 ppm (Chlorine). The inspector reminded the PIC that sanitzier buckets must be tested on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always between 50-200 ppm (Chlorine).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed fryer cleaner stored on the shelf above various food (including, but not limited to, seasonings). The PIC removed the cleaner from this location and placed it by the mop sink away from food. Ensure that toxic materials are stored away from food to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is not ingredients available for the pre-packaged items in the front display cooler (including, but not limited too, cakes, cookies, and other desserts). The inspector and PIC discussed keeping the original packaging with the ingredient list after the next shipment. The inspector suggests keeping all the ingredient lists in a binder by the cash register. Ensure that all foods packaged in the facility have labels available.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(A) Food Labels. (A) FOOD PACKAGED in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, shall be labeled as specified in LAW, including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following have exposed bare wood: (1) The end of the shelving holding spices above the pass-thru window; and (2) The edges of pass-thru window. The bare wood needs to be sealed (ex. paint) to create a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure these areas are sealed by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following physical facilities are not maintained in good repair: 

(1) The front area with the cash register requires cove base be added to the missing locations. 

(2) The cove base to the right of the back door and behind/around the triple sink needs to be sealed to the wall. 

(3) The corner wall edging to the right of cook line needs to be sealed to the wall. 

(4) The walls need to be repainted in food prep areas to be a light color. 

(5) The wall above the mirror in the bathroom needs to be sealed to the wall so there is not a gap. 

(6) There needs to be a self closer on the bathroom door. 

Ensure these physical facilities are repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.
